newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn 43 percent planted versus 42 average.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn 43 percent planted versus 42 average.

text.p: Missouri's corn crop was 43 percent planted as of Sunday, behind last year's 76 percent but just ahead of the five-year average, according to the weekly Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service report.
Soybeans were one percent planted, against three percent last year and two percent for the five-year average.
Wet fields hampered progress in the northern third of the state and 3.8 days were rated suitable for fieldwork.
Winter wheat was rated 11 percent poor, 29 percent fair, 48 percent good and 12 percent excellent, down slightly from a week earlier.
Twenty-one percent of the crop was headed, about five days ahead of the five-year average of 11 percent.
Oats were 95 percent planted, against 100 percent last year and the five-year average of 87 percent.
Grain sorghum was four percent planted, trailing nine percent for both last year and the five-year average.
Pasture and range condition was rated nine percent poor, 35 percent fair, 49 percent good and seven percent excellent, down slightly from the previous week.
Topsoil moisture was rated 10 percent short, 65 percent adequate and 25 percent surplus.
